day-52-act-01.title: Autoregressive Sampling: Greedy Decoding vs Temperature Scaling
day-52-act-01.prerequisites: Day 48 Decoder-Only Forward Pass and Day 41 Softmax.
day-52-act-01.objective: Formulate next-token prediction p_i = softmax(z_i / T) and explain how temperature T controls the entropy of the output distribution.
day-52-act-01.instructions: Given logits z = [2.0, 1.0, 0.0]: (1) Compute greedy argmax index 0. (2) Compute probabilities at T=1.0: exp([2,1,0]) = [7.389, 2.718, 1.0], sum=11.107 -> p = [0.665, 0.245, 0.090]. (3) Compute at T=0.5: z/0.5 = [4.0, 2.0, 0.0], exp([4,2,0]) = [54.598, 7.389, 1.0], sum=62.987 -> p = [0.867, 0.117, 0.016]. (4) Explain T -> 0 as greedy argmax and T -> inf as uniform.
day-52-act-01.exercise_prompt:
1. Compute softmax probabilities for z = [2.0, 1.0, 0.0] at T=2.0.
2. Why does low temperature (e.g. T=0.2) reduce hallucinations while increasing repetitive loops?
3. What runtime error occurs if T=0.0 is passed directly into division z / T?
day-52-act-01.answer: At T=2.0, p = [0.506, 0.307, 0.186]. Lower temperature squashes probability mass onto the highest logit, reducing surprise but causing cyclic repetition. T=0.0 causes ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero (code must route T=0 directly to argmax).
day-52-act-01.mastery_criterion: Derives temperature scaling analytically and explains the trade-off between diversity and repetition.

day-52-act-02.title: Truncation Strategies: Top-k and Nucleus (Top-p) Sampling
day-52-act-02.objective: Implement Top-k and Nucleus (Top-p) truncation algorithms and explain why Top-p adapts dynamically to distribution flatness.
day-52-act-02.instructions: Given sorted probabilities p = [0.40, 0.30, 0.15, 0.10, 0.05] for tokens A, B, C, D, E: (1) With k=2, truncate to {A, B} and renormalize to p = [0.4/0.7, 0.3/0.7] = [0.571, 0.429]. (2) With nucleus threshold p_cutoff=0.80, cumulative sums are A: 0.40, B: 0.70, C: 0.85 (>0.80) -> retain {A, B, C}, sum=0.85, renormalize to [0.471, 0.353, 0.176].
day-52-act-02.exercise_prompt:
1. What tokens are kept under Top-p with p=0.60?
2. What failure mode of Top-k does Top-p solve when the distribution is highly peaked (e.g. p = [0.98, 0.01, 0.01])?
3. State the algorithmic steps of Nucleus sampling in 3 lines.
day-52-act-02.hint: Cumulative sum: A is 0.40 (<0.60), A+B is 0.70 (>=0.60), so stop at B.
day-52-act-02.answer: With p=0.60, tokens {A, B} are kept (cumulative 0.70 >= 0.60). In peaked distributions, fixed k=5 forces the model to include low-quality tail tokens, while Top-p dynamically collapses to k=1. Steps: sort descending; compute cumsum; mask out tokens where cumsum shifted right > p; renormalize.
day-52-act-02.mastery_criterion: Accurately computes Top-p cutoffs and articulates the dynamic vocabulary advantage.

day-52-act-03.title: Repetition Penalties and Generation Invariance Under Random Seeds
day-52-act-03.objective: Apply multiplicative repetition penalty theta to logits and verify that fixing the random seed guarantees deterministic sampling traces.
day-52-act-03.instructions: For token i already present in the context, if logit z_i > 0, set z_i = z_i / theta; if z_i < 0, set z_i = z_i * theta (where theta > 1.0, e.g. 1.2). Verify that torch.manual_seed(42) produces identical generated token sequences across runs.
day-52-act-03.exercise_prompt:
1. Apply penalty theta=1.2 to generated logits z = [3.0, -2.0, 1.0] where token 0 and token 1 appeared previously.
2. Why is penalty division used for positive logits and multiplication for negative logits?
3. Write a two-line test demonstrating that seed=42 yields bitwise identical generated tokens.
day-52-act-03.answer: Penalized logits: [2.5, -2.4, 1.0]. Both operations reduce the logit (moving it further toward negative infinity), thereby decreasing the token's probability under softmax. Test: torch.manual_seed(42); seq1 = sample(); torch.manual_seed(42); seq2 = sample(); assert seq1 == seq2.
day-52-act-03.mastery_criterion: Applies penalty rules correctly and proves reproducibility via seed pinning.

day-52-act-04.title: Independent Sampling Strategy Implementation and Verification
day-52-act-04.objective: Write a complete generate() function in PyTorch implementing temperature, Top-k, and Top-p sampling with KV-cache / autoregressive loop.
day-52-act-04.instructions: Implement def generate(model, idx, max_new_tokens, temperature=1.0, top_k=None, top_p=None). Assert generated output matches expected shape (B, T + max_new_tokens).
day-52-act-04.exercise_prompt:
1. Provide the complete generate function code.
2. Verify that top_k=1 produces identical output to greedy argmax.
3. What guard is required when context length exceeds model block_size?
day-52-act-04.hint: Crop context: idx_cond = idx if idx.size(1) <= block_size else idx[:, -block_size:].
day-52-act-04.answer: def generate(model, idx, max_new_tokens, temperature=1.0, top_k=None, top_p=None): for _ in range(max_new_tokens): idx_cond = idx[:, -block_size:]; logits, _ = model(idx_cond); logits = logits[:, -1, :] / temperature; if top_k: v, _ = torch.topk(logits, top_k); logits[logits < v[:, [-1]]] = -float('Inf'); probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1); idx_next = torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1); idx = torch.cat((idx, idx_next), dim=1); return idx.
day-52-act-04.mastery_criterion: Fully functional generate function passing greedy equivalence and context cropping tests.
